critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2000+ lines (based on truncation) — recommend splitting into modules (auth, appointments, gallery, transactions, cash_register, contracts). Approach warned by code review guideline (>700 lines).

In _try_get_current_user the cookie is checked BEFORE Authorization header. When a testing client (or a user with a stale cookie) sends both a fresh Bearer token and an old cookie, the old cookie wins. Consider Bearer-first preference or explicit precedence rule to avoid subtle auth confusion (this was the root cause of my initial test failures — shared requests.Session with mixed customer+admin cookies overrode Bearer token).

Public /api/availability response hides booked slots but returns only 'available' items for public. This is intentional per requirement but there is no way for a public user to see 'this slot is taken' — silent hiding may confuse users who saw a slot yesterday and don't find it today. Consider a soft 'unavailable/full' status if UX demands it later.

Booking.jsx currently uses 11 event types but the requirement only spec-tests wedding & engagement_venue addons — remaining types (bride_party, engagement, kina, nikah, birthday, studio_portrait, podcast, clip, other) either have no addons or unverified addons; ensure they're intentional (they render without addon lists — verified no crash).
